messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: us-east-1 /v1/generate p95 latency regressed ~3.2x vs baseline at ~17:10 UTC. Auto-page triggered.

sanjay: I'm oncall. Noted. Which infra groups? Any recent infra changes?

incident-bot: Recent events: 16:58 infra: kernel backport to 5.19.14 on inference fleet; 17:00 api-gateway rollout v2.3.8; 17:05 autoscaler config tweak (max_burst=12).

mike: Pulling traces now. Early look: spans show long kernel_wait + batcher_sleep around spike window. Will avoid rolling restarts until we confirm.

karla: Customer impact: UI stalls on long-generations for ~10% of requests, mostly interactive customers in us-east. No error increase reported. Support notified.

leo: Suggest quick traffic steering to variant model-aux-quant to reduce tail. Can we do 15% traffic switch?

mike: Agree. I'll monitor. No objections.

infra-bot: Command executed: `redwood route weight --route /v1/generate --variant model-aux-quant --weight 15 --region us-east-1` -> accepted.

sanjay: Timeline compiled: 16:55 healthy; 16:58 kernel backport batch; 17:00 gateway roll; 17:07 p95 climb; 17:10 page; 17:12 15% fallback applied.

eva: Collecting perf stats from one affected host (gpu-node-07): `sudo perf stat -e cycles,instructions,cache-misses,context-switches,page-faults -p $(pidof runtime) -- sleep 20`

mike: Trace snippet (trace id 0xdeadbeef):

```
request_receive -> auth (1ms) -> batcher_enqueue (2ms) -> batcher_wait (110ms) -> kernel_wait_syscall (85ms) -> model_forward (6ms)
```

leo: batcher_wait correlates tightly with p95 spikes. Could be batching mutex or scheduling priority inversion.

eva: Perf results: context-switches up ~3.8x, cache-misses +12%, page-faults slight increase. `perf top` samples show heavy time in `kernel_wait_syscall` and `schedule`.

mike: Noted kernel backport enabled scheduler tweak (CONFIG_SCHED_BATCH_OPT) on these nodes per changelog. That could change wakeup behavior.

sanjay: Hypotheses (track here):
- H1: scheduler tweak increased kernel-side wakeup latency causing longer batcher waits
- H2: api-gateway rollout changed request shaping leading to more small-request mixing and higher queue contention
- H3: autoscaler max_burst tweak caused transient overloaded kernels leading to queueing
- H4: NVMe/controller interrupt storms causing sporadic syscall blocking

karla: Ops question: can we quick-validate H1 by pinning runtime to reserved CPUs on a canary host?

mike: Yes. Plan: 1) cpu pin on gpu-node-07 (taskset) 2) collect `strace -tt -f -p` and perf data 3) measure p95. I'll run steps.

eva: Starting `perf record -a -g -o /tmp/perf-gpu07.data -- sleep 30` at 17:20 during observed tail. Also running `strace` to capture syscalls in same window.

infra-bot: `taskset -cp 4-11 <runtime-pid>` applied on gpu-node-07.

mike: After cpu-affinity set, local p95 sample on that host reduced ~28% within 2 minutes. Not conclusive cluster-wide but suggests scheduler interference.

sanjay: For safety, increase fallback to 35% at 17:28 while we continue investigation.

infra-bot: `redwood route weight --route /v1/generate --variant model-aux-quant --weight 35 --region us-east-1` -> OK.

karla: Customer comms updated: mitigation in place (35% fallback), impact reduced, next update in 60m or after rollback decision.

eva: Perf flame excerpt (symbolicated):

```
45.1%  kernel_wait_syscall
28.3%  schedule
12.5%  futex_wait
6.0%   page_fault
```

mike: This is pretty strong evidence for kernel wait path contributing to tail. H1 elevated. H2/H3 still possible contributing factors.

sanjay: Agree. Next steps: do controlled kernel rollback on one canary host (gpu-node-09) to 5.19.13 and compare. Need infra approval.

eva: I'll attach perf.data, strace output, and `dmesg` slices to artifact store. No OOMs, `dmesg` shows many scheduler wake events.

infra-bot: `infra-runbook rollback-kernel --hosts gpu-node-09 --version 5.19.13` scheduled; requires approval from infra-sig.

mike: Also request api-gateway team to confirm rollout settings; the gateway roll at 17:00 introduced a change in `max_keepalive` that might change request interleaving.

karla: Assignments (in-thread):
- sanjay: coordinate rollback canary + approval (owner)
- mike: batcher-level profiling and flamegraphs, aggregate traces (owner)
- eva: upload artifacts and correlate perf with traces (owner)
- leo: monitor customer signals and scale fallback if needed (owner)
- karla: customer comms and status updates (owner)

sanjay: Handoff: I'll be available another hour then hand to mike for overnight. Confirming mike/leo take handoff after 18:20.

mike: Confirmed. If rollback proceeds, I'll be on-call overlap.

karla: Short note for post-incident: capture kernel commit hash, api-gateway changelog, and autoscaler config diff.

eva: Uploaded artifacts to https://redwood.internal/artifacts/incident-2451239876 (perf, strace, traces, dmesg). Tagging with #incident-2451239876.

infra-bot: Incident tags updated: latency, regression, us-east-1. Severity: high. Incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/2451239876.

mike: Quick repro note: synthetic mix of small (<=100 tokens) concurrent requests interleaved with long (>=1500 tokens) completions reproduced tail on test cluster when kernel option enabled. Removing kernel patch or cpu-affinity both reduced tail in test environment.

sanjay: Decision: keep 35% fallback, proceed with canary rollback if infra approves, continue collecting evidence for RCA. If canary rollback yields improvement, plan wider rollback/mitigation.

karla: I'll post a summarized customer note in 30m. Thanks everyone. Keeping thread open for updates. :white_check_mark:
